Starting today, Runna subscribers can use the new "Adapt for Heat" feature, which automatically adjusts pace targets based on local temperature and humidity. Details below.

Runna launches heat training tool

Personal running coach app Runna today announced three updates aimed at supporting users throughout their training cycle, from training in hot weather to post-race recovery.

From today, users can access the new "Adapt for Heat" feature, which will help users identify cooler running windows and suggest adjusted pace targets based on felt temperature, training duration, and specific sessions.

"Adapt for Heat" displays an hourly colour-coded weather forecast, letting users quickly find the best time to run and schedule training accordingly.

Here's Runna's introduction to this new feature:

Runna also announced the relaunch of its "Post-Race Recovery Plan" feature — once a user opens a 5K to 50K race plan, the system automatically generates a relevant programme. Runna's head coach and former Olympian Steph Kessell says these plans are designed by expert coaches to help runners "reduce the risk of burnout or injury".

Finally, the platform announced a new feature called "Upcoming Plans" launching in August. Users can queue up multiple training plans and automatically transition from one to the next upon completion, making long-term training scheduling more seamless.

Here's Runna's introduction to the benefits of "Upcoming Plans":

Plan your year in minutes: runners can overlay races, milestone goals, and training blocks, giving a clear view of the entire year. Zero admin between plans: no need to rebuild or start from scratch — when one plan ends, your preferred training schedule, predicted race times, and current fitness carry straight into the next. Flexible and fully in control: every plan can be edited, swapped, or removed at any time, with runners remaining fully in charge of their training experience. Built for progress: each plan is designed by Runna's expert coaches based on proven training principles to support sustainable progress, recovery, and race-day readiness.
